tacitus-card.jpg.note: AD 97, newly consul, on the wet Curia steps at night; bronze doors shut behind him, torches in iron brackets, bronze-cased scroll at his side. The rain solves the material problem BATCH_02 recorded - wool returns 60.8 specular pop against oiled leather's 124.3 - by soaking the toga until it goes dark and gleaming. Face is exactly the guard: lean, close-shaven, hair short and forward in the Trajanic manner, not a bearded philosopher. tacitus-terminal.jpg.note: About AD 116, twenty years on, writing the Annals alone by a two-wick bronze lamp. Pigeonholed scroll shelving behind, lamp smoke rising through the key, and a MARBLE BUST OF TIBERIUS on a plinth at the edge of the light, facing him - the emperor whose reign he is writing, watching him work. Toga removed and every highlight moved onto bronze, lamp oil and marble, which is why this plate holds its speculars where a wool-heavy one would not. ONE DEFECT ACCEPTED: he writes with a bronze stylus on parchment rather than cutting into wax - a stylus is a wax instrument. NOTE the audit reports key_side RIGHT while the lamp is plainly at the viewer's left; the bright white bust drags the bright centroid across. Radial key 0.208.

hannibal-terminal.jpg.note: The crossing of the Alps, October 218 BC - two years before Cannae, so BOTH EYES ARE STILL GOOD (he lost the sight of his right eye to ophthalmia in the Arno marshes in 217). Commissioned as a ROOM PORTRAIT in the manner of the Hume library plate: the invariant's shallow-focus background clause was deliberately reversed so the mountain reads as the subject and Hannibal is one small figure identifiable by the purple cloak. PASSED ALL FOUR ENFORCED RULES. THREE DEFECTS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY: the armour returned as ornate gilded filigree and the troops in uniform bronze helms, where the guard asked flatly for no fantasy armour; the elephant is gold-capped and healthy rather than the gaunt mud-caked animal specified, since nearly all of them died in the mountains; and the plate renders as digital painting rather than photograph. Also note it is the LIGHTEST plate in the deck at 10% of frame under 40/255 and mean luminance 119, taking that record from marcus-aurelius-terminal at 22%.

hannibal-card.jpg.note: New Carthage (Qart Hadasht) in Spain, spring 218 BC, aged 29, on the quay before the expedition. STRONGEST KEY IN THE DECK at radial 0.433, taking the record from musashi-card at 0.428. WHY NOT CARTHAGE: he left Carthage for Spain at nine - that departure is The Oath of Enmity, the first work in library/hannibal.json - and did not see the city again until he was forty-four. There is no handsome young adult Hannibal in Carthage. New Carthage is the city the Barcids built in Spain to be a second Carthage, funded by silver mines yielding three hundred pounds a day. LIKENESS: no bust or reliable coin survives, so the deck renders a characteristic face rather than a portrait, and takes the North African reading - deep brown skin, African features, Libyan and Numidian rather than Levantine. Carthage was an African city that had stood five hundred years among African peoples and married into them. BOTH EYES CLEAR, correct for 218: he loses the right one to ophthalmia in the Arno marshes the following year. TWO DEFECTS ACCEPTED: the temple on the hill reads Greco-Roman peripteral rather than Punic with an Egyptian cavetto cornice, and the houses read Mediterranean-modern rather than Punic. WEALTH BY DESIGN: Tyrian purple and gold on the man, silver pigs and shipping and a six-storey city behind him - richer than armour would have read, and it keeps the plate out of fantasy.

plato-card.jpg.note: Teaching at dusk on the plateau west of Athens, about 385 BC - seated at a low podium cutting a wax tablet, pupils in white chitons, a boy raking the sand, oil lamps in the sand, and the plateau dropping away to the Saronic Gulf with the lit Acropolis on the headland. REPLACES an earlier palaestra version and fixes its three faults: blown highlights went from 22% of frame to 0.0%, accent from 0.492 to 0.284, true shadow from 8% to 14%. NOTABLE - head_room measures 0.010, the FIRST NON-ZERO READING IN THE DECK. Every other plate reads 0.000 because something bright touches the top row; this one has genuine measured air above the figure, which is what the rewritten framing clause was for. TWO DEFECTS ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY. FIRST, the pupils are all open-mouthed and wide-eyed as though astonished, where the brief asked for thoughtful faces following a hard argument; at 340x560 in the codex those expressions read as comic. SECOND, it generated at 576x1024 - the second sub-2K roll running - so it is UPSAMPLED to 1120 where every other plate is downsampled from 2048.

plato-terminal.jpg.note: The Allegory of the Cave, Republic VII, as a ROOM PORTRAIT in the manner of the Alps and the Advocates Library - the invariant's shallow-focus background clause deliberately reversed so the cave reads as the subject. Prisoners chained at neck and ankle facing the wall, the raised walkway with figures carrying carved shapes on poles, the fire as the only real light, and the shadows enormous on the far wall as the largest thing in frame. Plato stands at the foot of the passage having come back down - the Republic requires the philosopher to return into the cave. Key reads LEFT, which is the fire, exactly as specified. Fails only on accent at 0.185, a hairline over the 0.18 ceiling on a firelit scene. TWO MINOR DEVIATIONS: Plato is roughly a third of the frame height rather than the under-a-fifth the brief asked for, and a lit candelabrum at the right edge introduces a second small light the brief did not call for.
